title: Autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: shipping sensible defaults and automated recommendations for batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles reduces per-token cost for common workloads while preserving latency SLOs. This PR wires together three pieces: a) new tuned defaults for the batcher and cache based on traffic signals, b) a small set of validated quantization profiles (FP16/INT8/AWQ) with runtime auto-selection heuristics, and c) a unit-economics tooling surface that surfaces recommended config changes in the Console and CLI autotune command. Summary of changes: - runtime: autotune heuristics + safe fallback when profiles fail - configs: new defaults.yaml with workload buckets and cache TTLs - quantization: profiles for common model families and runtime selection logic - tooling: CLI `redwood autotune` improvements and Console panel to preview cost impact - observability: new metrics for per-request unit cost and estimated savings - tests: added integration tests for profile selection and end-to-end cost calculations Checklist: - [x] Add tuned defaults and feature flag - [x] Add quantization profile catalog and runtime selection - [x] Add unit-econ metrics and Console panel - [x] Coverage for CI and flaky-e2e mitigation - [x] Docs and changelog items Notes: the autotune feature is behind feature flag `autotune_cost_defaults` and defaults to off for Dedicated deployments. The Console change is gated behind `uecon_ui_preview`. See linked Linear tickets for tuning data and perf benchmarks. Impact: measured ~18-28% token-cost reduction on mid-sized conversational workloads in lab canary with negligible tail-latency impact. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout + progressive enablement by org with telemetry check.

review_comments: Samir: Overall LGTM, great work. Two nits: make constants for the default TTLs and add a brief comment explaining the safety margin when falling back from INT8 to FP16.

Maya: Can you add one more assertion in the integration test to ensure the router falls back to the next-best profile when quantization fails at runtime? Also please ensure the Console panel respects feature flags.
Liam: Concern about autoscale interactions: do the batching defaults change node utilization in Dedicated? Recommend a short canary with same autoscale policy before broad rollout.

Ava (author): responded — added constants and comments, added fallback assertion to integration test, gated Console panel behind uecon_ui_preview flag, and added canary run notes to rollout plan in the PR description.
